337360.title: Degree-sum conjecture for matchings in 3-uniform hypergraphs with isolated vertices allowed
337360.statement:
Let $H$ be a $3$-graph of order $n$, let $s$ be an integer with $2\le s\le n/3$, and let $H_{n,3,s}^2$ and $H_{n,3,s}^3$ be the two extremal $3$-graphs used in the degree-sum comparison. **Piecewise degree-sum matching conjecture.** There exists $n_2\in\mathbb{N}$ such that, for $n\ge n_2$, if either

$$
sigma'_2(H)>\sigma'_2(H_{n,3,s}^2)\quad\text{and}\quad s\leq\frac{2n+4}{9},
$$

or

$$
sigma'_2(H)>\sigma'_2(H_{n,3,s}^3)\quad\text{and}\quad s>\frac{2n+4}{9},
$$

then $H$ contains a matching of size $s$. Unlike the preceding conjecture, this formulation allows isolated vertices; no resolution is supplied in the source context.
337360.source_name: Yi Zhang, Yi Zhao and Mei Lu, “Vertex degree sums for perfect matchings in 3-uniform hypergraphs”, arXiv:1710.04752 (2017).
337360.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.04752

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2017).

337500.title: KMS conjecture on finite presentability of finitely generated Lambda-free groups
337500.statement: Let $\Lambda$ be an ordered abelian group, and let $G$ be a finitely generated group acting freely on a $\Lambda$-tree; such a group is called **$\Lambda$-free**. **KMS conjecture.** Every finitely generated $\Lambda$-free group is finitely presented. If true, this would imply that all finitely generated $\Lambda$-free groups are $\mathbb{R}^n$-free. The source presents this as an open conjecture attributed to KMS12.
337500.source_name: Olga Kharlampovich and Alina Vdovina, “Beyond Serre's "Trees" in two directions: Λ–trees and products of trees”, arXiv:1710.10306 (2017).
337500.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.10306

Status: **open** according to the source (as of October 2017).

337501.title: Caprace's polynomial bound conjecture for arithmetic lattices on products of two trees
337501.statement: Let $q$ denote the parameter in the family of arithmetic lattices under consideration, and consider arithmetic lattices acting simply transitively on a product of two trees. **Caprace's conjecture.** The number of non-commensurable arithmetic lattices acting simply transitively on a product of two trees is bounded polynomially in $q$. The source gives no resolution or further qualifications for this conjecture.
337501.source_name: Olga Kharlampovich and Alina Vdovina, “Beyond Serre's "Trees" in two directions: Λ–trees and products of trees”, arXiv:1710.10306 (2017).
337501.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.10306

Status: **open** according to the source (as of October 2017).

337505.title: Ur-equivalence determined by the original and deleted posets
337505.statement:
Let $P$ and $Q$ be posets, with elements $x\in P$ and $y\in Q$. Write $P[x\to\varnothing]$ and $Q[y\to\varnothing]$ for the posets obtained by applying the Ur-operation at $x$ and $y$, respectively, and write $\sim$ for isomorphism. **Ur-equivalence conjecture.** The elements $x$ and $y$ are Ur-equivalent if and only if

$$
P\sim Q\quad\text{and}\quad P[x\to\varnothing]\sim Q[y\to\varnothing].
$$

The claim proposes that Ur-equivalence is completely determined by the isomorphism types of the original posets and the posets obtained by applying the Ur-operation at the distinguished elements. The surrounding discussion presents it as a possible strengthening of the preceding corollary, with no resolution supplied here.
337505.source_name: Thomas Browning, Max Hopkins and Zander Kelley, “Doppelgangers: the Ur-Operation and Posets of Bounded Height”, arXiv:1710.10407 (2018).
337505.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.10407

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2017).

337521.title: Finite-order conjecture for the Coxeter transformation of cominuscule posets
337521.statement:
Let $\Phi$ be one of the root systems of type $A$, $B$, $C$, $D$, $E_6$, or $E_7$, and let $\mathsf{C}$ be a cominuscule poset. Write $\mathsf{J(C)}$ for its poset of order ideals, and let $\tau$ denote the Auslander–Reiten translation on the Grothendieck group of the bounded derived category of the incidence algebra of $\mathsf{J(C)}$. Here $h$ is the Coxeter number of the relevant root system.

**Finite-order conjecture.** The translation $\tau$ has finite order, specifically

$$
\tau^{2(h+1)}=\operatorname{id}.
$$

This predicts a uniform periodicity for the Coxeter transformation associated with incidence algebras of cominuscule posets across the listed root-system types. The supplied text gives no evidence that the conjecture has been proved or disproved.
337521.source_name: Emine Yildirim, “The Coxeter transformation on Cominuscule Posets”, arXiv:1710.10632 (2018).
337521.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.10632

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2017).

337671.title: Minimal-degree conjecture for intervals in the Tamari lattice
337671.statement: Let $\operatorname{\mathbf{Tam}}_n$ be the Tamari lattice, and let $\mathbb{D}_n$ be its refined interval polynomial in variables $x,y,\overline{x},\overline{y}$. An interval has degree $n-1$ in $(x,y,\overline{y},\overline{x})$ when the corresponding monomial has total degree $n-1$ in these four variables; call $(S,S)$ a **simple interval**. **Minimal-degree conjecture.** The only intervals of degree $n-1$ in $(x,y,\overline{y},\overline{x})$ are the simple intervals $(S,S)$. The preceding proposition establishes the lower bound $n-1$ for the degree in $(x,y,\overline{y})$, while the source gives no resolution of this four-variable claim.
337671.source_name: Frédéric Chapoton, “A note on Tamari intervals”, arXiv:1711.05027 (2017).
337671.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.05027

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2017).

337702.title: Harutyunyan's half-degree conjecture for regular digraphs
337702.statement:
Let $D$ be a $k$-regular digraph, meaning that every vertex has in-degree and out-degree $k$. Its chromatic number is denoted by $\chi(D)$.

**Harutyunyan's conjecture.** One has

$$
\chi(D)\leq\left\lceil\frac{k}{2}\right\rceil+1.
$$

This is presented as an upper bound improving the general bound $\chi(D)\leq\min\{\Delta^+(D),\Delta^-(D)\}+1$ for regular digraphs. The source does not specify whether the conjecture has been resolved.
337702.source_name: Saeed Akbari, Amir Hossein Ghodrati, Afrouz Jabalameli and Morteza Saghafian, “Chromatic Number and Dichromatic Polynomial of Digraphs”, arXiv:1711.06293 (2017).
337702.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.06293

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2017).

337703.title: Cichacz–Görlich–Tuza conjecture on cordial hypertrees
337703.statement: Let $H=(V,E)$ be a hypertree, meaning a connected hypergraph without cycles. A vertex labeling $f:V\to\mathbb{Z}_2$ induces an edge labeling by $f(e)=\sum_{v\in e}f(v)$ modulo $2$. The hypergraph is **$2$-cordial** when the numbers of vertices and edges receiving the two labels differ by at most $1$. **Cichacz–Görlich–Tuza's conjecture.** Every hypertree is $2$-cordial. The paper proves this statement, as part of the stronger result that every hypertree is $k$-cordial for $k\in\{2,3\}$.
337703.source_name: Michał Tuczyński, Przemysław Wenus and Krzysztof Węsek, “On cordial labeling of hypertrees”, arXiv:1711.06294 (2019).
337703.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.06294

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2017). “For other values of $k$, the conjecture is still open.”

337705.title: 2-cordiality conjecture for 1-degenerate connected hypergraphs
337705.statement: Let $H$ be a connected hypergraph. It is **$1$-degenerated** if every subhypergraph of $H$ has a vertex of degree at most $1$. A hypergraph is $2$-cordial when a labeling of its vertices by $\mathbb{Z}_2$, with each edge labeled by the sum modulo $2$ of the labels of its vertices, makes the numbers of vertices and edges receiving the two labels differ by at most $1$. **1-degenerate hypergraph cordiality conjecture.** Every $1$-degenerated connected hypergraph is $2$-cordial. The paper identifies this as a natural next step beyond its proof that all hypertrees are $2$-cordial; its status is left open.
337705.source_name: Michał Tuczyński, Przemysław Wenus and Krzysztof Węsek, “On cordial labeling of hypertrees”, arXiv:1711.06294 (2019).
337705.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.06294

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2017). “For other values of $k$, the conjecture is still open.”

337785.title: Nonnegative Demazure-character expansion for Kohnert polynomials of Demazure diagrams
337785.statement: Let $D$ be a demazure diagram, meaning a finite cell diagram satisfying the demazure condition described in the paper, and let ${\mathfrak K}_D$ denote its Kohnert polynomial. **The nonnegative expansion conjecture.** The polynomial ${\mathfrak K}_D$ expands as a nonnegative sum of Demazure characters. This is motivated by the fact that both composition diagrams and Rothe diagrams are demazure, and by extensive computations supporting the claim.
337785.source_name: Sami Assaf and Dominic Searles, “Kohnert polynomials”, arXiv:1711.09498 (2018).
337785.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.09498

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of November 2017). “While this coincidence of skew polynomials and Schubert polynomials does not hold in general, we conjecture that Schubert polynomials are, in fact, nested between Demazure characters and skew polynomials in the following sense.”

337814.title: Bao Shou's same-fingerprint symbol-invariant conjecture
337814.statement: Let rigid semisimple operators be labeled by pairs of partitions $(\lambda^{'},\lambda^{”})$. Fix a fingerprint invariant, and consider operators satisfying different conditions in the definition of that fingerprint. **Bao Shou's same-fingerprint symbol-invariant conjecture.** Rigid semisimple operators with the same fingerprint invariant and satisfying different conditions in the definition of the fingerprint have the same symbol invariant. This is presented as the strategy needed to prove that the fingerprint invariant implies the symbol invariant; the source does not state whether the conjecture has been proved or disproved.
337814.source_name: Chuanzhong Li and Bao Shou, “Invariants of rigid surface operators”, arXiv:1711.10356 (2024).
337814.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.10356

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2017).

337824.title: Non-separating cycle with a nowhere-zero 4-flow conjecture
337824.statement: Let $G$ be a cyclically $4$-edge connected cubic graph. For a cycle $C$ of $G$, let $G/E(C)$ denote the graph obtained by contracting the edges of $C$, and let a **nowhere-zero $4$-flow** mean a nowhere-zero flow over a group of order $4$. **Non-separating cycle with a nowhere-zero $4$-flow conjecture.** The graph $G$ contains a non-separating cycle $C$ such that $G/E(C)$ has a nowhere-zero $4$-flow. The source states that this conjecture would imply the cycle double cover conjecture and, in particular, the $5$-cycle double cover conjecture.
337824.source_name: Arthur Hoffmann-Ostenhof, Cun-Quan Zhang and Zhang Zhang, “Cycle double covers and non-separating cycles”, arXiv:1711.10614 (2018).
337824.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.10614

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2017).

337839.title: Ek's recurrence conjecture for restricted-partition polynomials
337839.statement:
Let $G_s(n,k)$ be the polynomial defined by summing over partitions $(d_1,\ldots,d_k)$ satisfying $\sum_{i=1}^k i d_i=k$ and $\sum_{i=1}^k d_i\leq s$, with the recurrence described above. **Ek's recurrence conjecture.** For $G_s(n,k)$, the recurrence relation

$$
q^n(q^{k+s}-1)G_s(n+1,k)-q^{k+1}(q^n-q^{s-2})G_s(n,k+1)+(q^n-q^{k+s-1})G_s(n+1,k+1)=0.
$$

This conjecture extends the experimentally observed order-one, degree-one recurrence relations found for $s=1,2,3,4$ to general $s$. Its status is not determined by the supplied text.
337839.source_name: Bryan Ek, “q-Binomials and related symmetric unimodal polynomials”, arXiv:1711.11252 (2018).
337839.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.11252

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2017).

337847.title: VC-density conjecture for subgraphs of Cartesian products
337847.statement:
Let $G$ be a subgraph of the Cartesian product

$$
G_1\square\cdots\square G_m.
$$

Here, $\operatorname{VC-dens}^*(G)$ denotes the VC-density of $G$. **VC-density conjecture.**

$$
\frac{|E(G)|}{|V(G)|}\le \operatorname{VC-dens}^*(G).
$$

The conjecture strengthens the paper's density bounds for subgraphs of Cartesian products, which relate edge density to the VC-dimension and to the densities of the factors. Its status is not specified in the supplied text.
337847.source_name: Victor Chepoi, Arnaud Labourel and Sébastien Ratel, “On density of subgraphs of Cartesian products”, arXiv:1711.11485 (2019).
337847.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.11485

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2017).

337876.title: The NonKrupp subarrangement conjecture for pseudocircle arrangements
337876.statement:
Let ${\cal A}$ be a connected digon-free arrangement of pseudocircles. A triple of pseudocircles forms a triangle in ${\cal A}$ when its three pseudocircles bound such a triangular cell, and it is **NonKrupp** when it is not a Krupp configuration. Let ${\cal N}_6^\Delta$ denote the specified arrangement of six pseudocircles.

**NonKrupp subarrangement conjecture.** If every triple of pseudocircles which forms a triangle in ${\cal A}$ is NonKrupp, then ${\cal A}$ contains ${\cal N}_6^\Delta$ as a subarrangement.

All arrangements known to be non-circularizable by the stated theorem contain ${\cal N}_6^\Delta$ as a subarrangement, motivating this conjecture. Its resolution is not given in the source.
337876.source_name: Stefan Felsner and Manfred Scheucher, “Arrangements of Pseudocircles: On Circularizability”, arXiv:1712.02149 (2020).
337876.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.02149

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2017).

337901.title: Abyazi Sani–Alishahi conjecture for deleted Kneser hypergraphs
337901.statement:
Let $A\subset[n]$, and let $\mathrm{KG}^r_A(n,k)$ be the subhypergraph of the $r$-uniform Kneser hypergraph induced by the $k$-subsets $\sigma\subset[n]$ with $\sigma\not\subset A$. **Abyazi Sani–Alishahi's conjecture.** If $n\ge 2rk$, then

$$
\chi\bigl(\mathrm{KG}^r_A(n,k)\bigr)=\left\lceil\frac{n-\max\{r(k-1),|A|\}}{r-1}\right\rceil.
$$

The source identifies this as a conjecture of Abyazi Sani and Alishahi and does not state a general resolution.
337901.source_name: Jai Aslam, Shuli Chen, Ethan Coldren, Florian Frick and Linus Setiabrata, “On the generalized Erdős–Kneser conjecture: proofs and reductions”, arXiv:1712.03456 (2017).
337901.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.03456

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of December 2017). “This was proven by Alon, Frankl, and Lov\'asz .”

337912.title: The Saxl graph diameter-two conjecture for primitive base-two groups
337912.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite primitive permutation group with base size $b(G)=2$, and let $\alpha0\Sigma(G)$ be its Saxl graph, whose vertices are the points of the permutation domain and whose edges join pairs forming a base. **The Saxl graph diameter-two conjecture.** Either $G$ is a Frobenius group and $\alpha0\Sigma(G)$ is complete, or

$$
\operatorname{diam}(\Sigma(G))=2.
$$

This conjecture asserts that, apart from the complete Saxl graphs arising from primitive Frobenius groups, primitive base-two groups have highly connected Saxl graphs. It is presented as an open problem in the source.
337912.source_name: Timothy C. Burness and Michael Giudici, “On the Saxl graph of a permutation group”, arXiv:1712.03688 (2018).
337912.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.03688

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2017).

337932.title: The unimodality conjecture for Euclid polynomials
337932.statement: Let $E_k(\lambda)$ be the Euclid polynomials. A polynomial $p(\lambda)=\sum_{j=0}^{n}a_j\lambda^j$ is **unimodal** when its coefficient vector $[a_0,a_1,\ldots,a_n]$ consists of positive integers that first increases monotonically to a peak, possibly attained at two or more adjacent coefficients, and then decreases monotonically to $a_n=1$. **Unimodality conjecture.** The Euclid polynomials are unimodal. The first four Euclid polynomials are stated to have this property, but no general proof or resolution is supplied in the provided text.
337932.source_name: Eunice Y. S. Chan and Robert M. Corless, “Minimal height companion matrices for Euclid polynomials”, arXiv:1712.04405 (2017).
337932.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.04405

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2017).

338006.title: Weakly convex domination can decrease under permutation in diameter-two graphs
338006.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph with $\operatorname{diam}(G)=2$, and let $\pi$ be a permutation of its vertex set $V_G$. Write $\gamma_{wcon}(G)$ for the weakly convex domination number of $G$, and let $\pi G$ denote the corresponding permuted prism graph. **Weakly convex domination decrease conjecture.** There exist $G$ and $\pi$ such that

$$
\gamma_{wcon}(G)=\left|V_G\right| \qquad\text{and}\qquad \gamma_{wcon}(\pi G)<\gamma_{wcon}(G).
$$

The conjecture proposes that, unlike the established convex-domination behavior in the relevant setting, a permutation can strictly lower the weakly convex domination number even when the original connected graph has diameter two. The supplied text gives no resolution.
338006.source_name: Monika Rosicka, “Convex and weakly convex domination in prism graphs”, arXiv:1712.07545 (2017).
338006.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.07545

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2017).

355592.title: Characteristic-polynomial conjecture for parameter matrices of hypergraph transversals
355592.statement:
Let $\mathbb{S}$ be the parameter matrix of a $k$-transversal in a $d$-uniform $r$-regular hypergraph $\mathcal{G}$. Let $\xi$ be a $d$-th primitive root of unity. **Characteristic-polynomial conjecture.** The characteristic polynomial of $\mathbb{S}$ is

$$
\varphi(\lambda)=\lambda^{d-2}\prod\limits_{i=j}^d(\lambda-\xi^{jk}r).
$$

The preceding result identifies the eigenvalues of the parameter matrix; this conjecture further specifies their algebraic multiplicities through the characteristic polynomial. The source also notes the belief that all nonzero eigenvalues have the same algebraic multiplicity, but provides no resolution of the conjecture.
355592.source_name: Anna A. Taranenko, “Perfect colorings of hypergraphs”, arXiv:2208.03447 (2024).
355592.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2017–2022). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1705.03709](https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.03709).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.03447

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2022).
